t.5.22.1: Then the rākṣasī women with hideous faces, harsh themselves, approached Sītā and spoke to her harsh and unpleasant words.
t.5.22.2: O Sītā, you who enchant the hearts of all beings, why do you not consent to dwell in my inner palace, furnished with costly couches?
t.5.22.3: Being a mortal woman, you set great store by being the wife of a mere mortal man. Withdraw your mind from Rāma, or you will never live on.
t.5.22.4: Being a human woman, O lovely one, you desire that human Rāma, but he is fallen from his kingdom, his aims unfulfilled, and helpless, O faultless lady.
t.5.22.5: Having heard the words of the Rākṣasīs, lotus-eyed Sītā, her eyes filled with tears, spoke these words.
t.5.22.7: A human woman is not fit to become the wife of a rākṣasa. Devour me, all of you, if you wish; I will not do as you say. Whether he is wretched or bereft of his kingdom, he who is my husband is my revered master.
t.5.22.6: This speech, hateful to the world, which you utter as you stand gathered together, this sinful word finds no place in my mind.
t.5.22.8: Having heard Sītā's words, the rākṣasīs, overcome with rage and urged on by Rāvaṇa, threatened her with harsh words.
t.5.22.9: Hidden in the śiṃśapā tree, silent, the monkey Hanumān heard those rākṣasīs threatening Sītā.
t.5.22.10: Approaching her from all sides as she trembled, the enraged ones fiercely licked their blazing, hanging lips.
t.5.22.11: And, utterly enraged, they quickly seized their axes and said: "She does not deserve Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, as her husband."
t.5.22.12: Being threatened by the fearsome rākṣasīs, she of the lovely face, wiping away her tears, approached that śiṃśapā tree.
t.5.22.13: Then wide-eyed Sītā, surrounded by the rākṣasīs, approached that śiṃśapā tree and stood there, overwhelmed with grief.
t.5.22.14: Those fearsome rākṣasīs, surrounding her on all sides, began to threaten her, emaciated, sad-faced, and wearing soiled garments.
t.5.22.15: Then a rākṣasī named Vinatā, terrible to behold, hideous, with a sunken belly and an angry look, spoke to her.
t.5.22.16: Sītā, this much is enough; you have shown your love for your husband. Everywhere, good lady, what is carried to excess leads to ruin.
t.5.22.17: I am well pleased with you, good fortune be yours; you have observed the conduct proper to humans. But now, Maithilī, act also upon the wholesome words that I am speaking.
t.5.22.18: Accept Rāvaṇa as your husband, the lord of all the rākṣasas, valiant and handsome, like Vāsava, lord of the gods.
t.5.22.19: Abandon Rāma, a wretched mortal, and take refuge with Rāvaṇa, who is courteous, generous by nature, and speaks pleasantly to everyone.
t.5.22.21: What use is Rāma to you, O Vaidehī, that wretched man whose life is spent?
t.5.22.20: O Vaidehī, anointed with divine unguents and adorned with divine ornaments, from this day forth be the sovereign mistress of all the worlds, O lovely one, as the goddess Svāhā is of Agni, or as Śacī is of Indra.
t.5.22.22: If you do not carry out these words that I have spoken, we will all devour you this very moment.
t.5.22.23: But another, named Vikaṭā, with hanging breasts, enraged, raised her fist and, roaring, spoke to Sītā.
t.5.22.24: O most foolish one, out of compassion and gentleness we have endured many improper words of yours, O Maithilī, yet you do not follow our counsel, which is beneficial and suited to the time.
t.5.22.25: You have been brought to the far shore of the ocean, hard for others to reach, and you have entered the terrible inner palace of Rāvaṇa, O Maithilī.
t.5.22.26: Confined in the house of Rāvaṇa and closely guarded by us, you cannot be rescued even by Puraṃdara himself.
t.5.22.27: O Maithilī, do as I say, for I speak for your good. Enough of shedding tears; give up this useless grief.
t.5.22.28: Embrace love and delight, and cast off this constant wretchedness. O Sītā, sport with the king of the rākṣasas as you please.
t.5.22.29: For you know, timid one, how unstable the youth of women is; so long as yours has not passed away, enjoy happiness.
t.5.22.30: O woman with intoxicating eyes, roam with the king of the Rākṣasas through delightful gardens and the groves upon the mountains.
t.5.22.31: Seven thousand women will stand under your command, O lovely one; accept Rāvaṇa as your husband, the lord of all the rākṣasas.
t.5.22.32: Or else, Maithilī, I will tear out your heart and devour it, if you do not carry out properly the words I have spoken.
t.5.22.33: Then the rākṣasī named Caṇḍodarī, fearsome to behold, brandishing a great spear, spoke these words.
t.5.22.34: Seeing this woman, with eyes tremulous as a deer's and breasts quivering with fear, carried off by Rāvaṇa, a great craving arose in me.
t.5.22.36: Then a rākṣasī named Praghasā spoke these words: "Let us squeeze the throat of this cruel woman! Why do we sit idle?"
t.5.22.35: The liver and the spleen, then the swelling flesh of the breast, and the heart together with its ligaments, the entrails as well, and likewise the head: these I would devour. Such is my mind.
t.5.22.37: Then let it be reported to the king that the human woman has died. There is no doubt at all about this: he will say, "Eat her!"
t.5.22.38: Then the rākṣasī named Ajāmukhī spoke these words: “Cut her to pieces, and then make all the lumps of flesh equal in size.”
t.5.22.40: Then the rākṣasī named Śūrpaṇakhā spoke these words: "What has been said by Ajāmukhī, that indeed is pleasing to me."
t.5.22.39: Then let us all divide her up; quarrelling does not please me. Let drink be brought quickly, and many garlands of various kinds.
t.5.22.42: Thus being threatened by the most dreadful rākṣasīs, Sītā, who was like a daughter of the gods, abandoned her composure and wept.
t.5.22.41: And let wine, which destroys all sorrow, be brought quickly. Having obtained human flesh, we shall then dance before Nikumbhilā.
